original_question: Let p be the number of distinct processing times. Are each of the three preemptive parallel-machine problems P|pmtn,r_j|sum C_j, P|pmtn|sum U_j, and P|pmtn|sum T_j fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by p?
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the correct target: the exact three preemptive parallel-identical-machine problems discussed immediately before Open Problem 9, and the intended parameter is indeed the number of distinct processing times. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1709.01670))
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone, it should explicitly say that P denotes parallel identical machines, not arbitrary parallel or unrelated machines.

The parameter should be defined unambiguously as p := |{p_j : j in J}|, the cardinality of the set of distinct job processing times; otherwise p can be confused with an individual processing time symbol p_j.
The symbols in the three-field notation should be unpacked: pmtn means preemption is allowed, and r_j means each job j has a release date before which it cannot start.
The objective terms should be defined: C_j is the completion time of job j; for due date d_j, U_j = 1 if C_j > d_j and U_j = 0 otherwise; T_j = max{C_j - d_j, 0}.
It should note that these are the unweighted versions of the objectives; the paper's notation suppresses weights here.

If the question is meant to be self-contained in parameterized-complexity language, it should specify that 'fixed-parameter tractable' means solvable in time f(p)·|I|^{O(1)} for some computable function f on instances I.

The paper poses this as one grouped open problem about those three named problems, after observing that the equal-processing-time special cases are polynomial-time solvable; including that nearby motivation makes the reformulation more faithful to the paper's intent.
refined_question: Let J be a set of jobs to be scheduled on m parallel identical machines, with preemption allowed, and let p := |{p_j : j in J}| be the number of distinct job processing times. Is each of the following optimization problems fixed-parameter tractable with respect to p, that is, solvable in time f(p)·|I|^{O(1)} for some computable function f: (i) P|pmtn,r_j|∑_{j in J} C_j, where each job j has release date r_j and completion time C_j; (ii) P|pmtn|∑_{j in J} U_j, where each job j has due date d_j and U_j = 1 iff C_j > d_j; and (iii) P|pmtn|∑_{j in J} T_j, where T_j = max{C_j - d_j, 0}?
justification: This draft is targeting exactly Open Problem 9 in Section 4.5. In that subsection, the authors first name the three problems P|pmtn,r_j|∑C_j, P|pmtn|∑U_j, and P|pmtn|∑T_j, note that they are NP-hard while the equal-processing-time special cases are polynomial-time solvable, and then ask: are the above problems fixed-parameter tractable parameterized by the number of distinct processing times? The extra definitions needed to make your draft fully stand-alone come from the paper's preliminaries: Section 2.1.1 defines P as parallel identical machines, Section 2.1.2 defines r_j and pmtn, Section 2.1.3 defines C_j, U_j, and T_j and explains that the unweighted variants drop the weight symbol, and Section 2.2 gives the standard meaning of fixed-parameter tractability. The fetched HTML exposes the exact section/label locations, and the arXiv abstract page gives the journal reference 100:254-261, but page-local numbering is not exposed in the HTML fetch. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1709.01670))
